events.title: Intermediate Sewing Machine Skills: Mini Puff Quilt
events.description: Make a mini puff quilt (4 or 9 patches) to use as a decorative pillow – or, keep going on your own and make a whole quilt! Materials provided. Collaborator: Textile Center. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund. This is an intermediate level sewing class; participants should have some basic experience using a sewing machine. Class is limited to 8 people on a first-come, first-served basis. Arrive a few minutes early to sign up for a spot. The RKMC Room is located on the Skyway level of the library. Access via the escalator or elevator from the Library Atrium.  The class will run concurrently with the Minneapolis Central Craft Club program across the hall, so people could participate in Craft Club and work on a different crafting project if the sewing class is full.

events.title: Baile latino para adultos / Latin Dance for Adults
events.description: ¡Acompáñenos en una introducción a los bailes latinos! Únase con nosotros para explorar el movimiento y la autoexpresión a través de bailes latinos, como la salsa. Todas las personas son bienvenidas sin importar su habilidad de baile; Proporcionaremos modificaciones al baile para aquellas personas con limitaciones físicas o de otro tipo. La clase se llevará a cabo en español e inglés. Colaborador: Nela Dance. Este programa es financiado por el Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund. Join us for an introduction to Latin Dance! Come together for movement and self-expression as we engage in Latin dance such as salsa. All skill levels and abilities welcome; modifications available. The class will be taught in Spanish and English. Collaborator: Nela Dance. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund. Collaborator: Nela Dance. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund.

Or have a particular online, email, formatting or printing issue that needs assistance? A computer tutor volunteer will be available at the library to offer aid and guide you in completing your task. Drop-ins are welcome on a first-come, first-served basis. Please note your computer needs must be limited in time but we will try at least to get you started in the right direction. Call 612-543-8400 before you arrive if you want to confirm the tutor’s availability. Runs 2026-08-26 through 2026-09-30.

events.title: Darning 101
events.description: Rips and holes can happen in our favorite knit garments, including T-shirts, socks, and workout clothes. Heal all of those holes with darning and community during this 2-hour class. Learn how to repair knit garments using two methods of darning. Previous darning skills not required. Fine motor skills used in class. Materials provided. Collaborator: Curiosity Studio. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund.

events.title: Tech Help for Seniors
events.description: Seniors, get one-on-one technology support for your personal device (smartphone, tablet or laptop). This program is staffed by tech support volunteers with expertise in working with adults age 60 and older to navigate the digital landscape. Bring your own device, or a library computer will be available. Registration required. Please call the library at 612-543-5800 to make an appointment for one 45-minute session. Registration is limited. If you need to cancel your appointment, please call the library to open a spot for another patron. Collaborator: Senior Community Services (SCS). Please note: This Tech Help for Seniors program with SCS is for people age 60+. You must be registered with SCS to attend an appointment; registration is free. This age limit is a condition of the funding for this program provided by the State of Minnesota Department of Human Services. If you are younger than 60, please see the additional Tech Help programs provided at other Hennepin County libraries. Runs 2026-08-25 through 2026-09-01.

events.title: Protection Charm With Traditional Korean Patchwork
events.description: These classes center on the theme, "The Art of Being With...," and are related to the exhibit at Minneapolis Central Library. Together, they explore the idea that giving and receiving care and love brings meaning to our lives. Thoughtfulness is essential in finding purpose; without it, everyday moments can feel less significant. Rather than focusing on technical skills, each class highlights the meaningful act of creating objects that reflect care. Participants will work with ceramic painting and traditional textile elements to practice thoughtfulness and express care for themselves and others. No previous experience is needed; all skill levels are welcome. In session one of the two-part series, participants will paint and work with textiles. In session two, textile work will be incorporated and ceramic pieces will be painted and assembled into the finished object. Materials provided. Register for both sessions. This program is funded with money from Minnesota’s Arts and Cultural Heritage Fund. September 12 : Painting on ceramic pollack + sewing Jogakbo. Cultural significance: In a custom called Bugeo Aekmaegi, dried pollack uses its wide-open eyes and mouth to watch for evil spirits and swallow misfortune. This is paired with Jogakbo (patchwork), the traditional Korean art of "wrapping luck" and fortune. September 26 : Painting on ceramic old coin + sewing Jogakbo. Cultural significance: These represent Byeoljeon, rare commemorative coins gifted by mothers to marrying daughters on decorative key pendants to wish for marital harmony and prosperity. This is paired with Jogakbo patchwork to wrap and hold that family fortune together. View The Art of Being With: Light, Shadow, Wind and Body exhibit – on display August 8-September 27 in Cargill Gallery on the second floor of Minneapolis Central Library.

Join us at the McGregor Library for our Relaxed Readers book club! We get together in the Library's meeting room to talk about everything we're reading. events.title: Music Under the Pines: Bill and Julie Kaiser
events.description: LIVE MUSIC at the Forest Inn!   The Kaisers have entertained audiences at Itasca State Park for over 20 years! Bill and Julie perform favorites from across the decades in smooth harmonies backed by intricate acoustic guitar.  This is an indoor event. Seating is provided. The Music Under the Pines summer concert series is sponsored in partnership with the Friends of Itasca State Park.

events.title: Shovel Point - Guided Hike
events.description: Take a hike with a Naturalist out to Shovel Point and enjoy panoramic views of Lake Superior and its shoreline. We�‚’ll discuss the fiery formation of this landscape, some of the plants and animals that make this harsh climate their home, and we will spend time talking about anything else that pops to mind! The hike is 1.5 miles long and will meet at the Visitor Center. Bring sunscreen and sturdy shoes!

events.title: Birding in the Big Woods
events.description: Many species of colorful birds call the Big Woods home. Learn the basics of bird identification and test out your new skills on an easy half mile naturalist led hike.  A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Meet at the picnic shelter. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Science of Skulls
events.description: Is it a predator or prey? Does it eat plants or meat? Skulls can tell us a lot about the animals to which they belong. Stop by picnic shelter anytime between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. to see what you might discover! This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Summer Concert: Good Ol' Tom
events.description: Meet at the Amphitheater.  The Friends of Lake Bemidji State Park and the North Country Snowmobile Club present our annual Music Under the Pines summer concert series.  Come out to enjoy guitar and sing-along music by Good Ol' Tom. Concerts are held at our outdoor amphitheater under the tall pine trees. If it is raining, it will be held inside the Visitor Center.

events.title: Jr. Naturalist: Mississippi Headwaters River Walk
events.description: Meet at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center. Kids and families, come walk in the water and explore the first stretch of the Mississippi River. This walk in the river will investigate and search for the critters and plants that live along this water trail.  Notes: Wear clothes that can get wet, wear water shoes to protect your feet. Water is quite shallow 1-2 ft in depth but may be deeper in some sections. Small children may need to have life jackets. Adults must accompany children.

events.title: Who Livesss Here?- Snake Habitat Exploration Nature Table
events.description: Have you ever heard a slithery rustle in the grass while out hiking   or nearly tripped on a rope-like reptile? Were you left shaken wondering what type of snake you came across or if you were in harm's way? William O'Brien is home to at least 7 snake species that have all adapted to thrive in their own individual habitats. Familiarize yourself with snakes found in the park and learn about how to safely interact with our scaly friends. No live snakes will be present.  Drop by the naturalist table at the visitor center.

events.title: Slithering Friends
events.description: St Croix State Park is home to ten different species of snakes, each with their own unique appearance! Come join us in making a snake-inspired craft and explore all the special features of different snake species.

events.title: Written in Stone
events.description: It's not just a rock - it's a clue!  Rocks hold the secrets of the earth, trapping clues of time and place as they form.  Millions of years later we can use these clues to discover ancient worlds that used to exist right here at Banning State Park.

events.title: Monarch Butterfly Tagging
events.description: Every year, monarch butterflies undertake an incredible migration. Scientists tag monarch butterflies to learn more about them as they make their way south. Participate in citizen science with a naturalist and learn first-hand how to tag monarch butterflies.  If interested, meet at the Picnic Shelter on the Waterfall side of the park.  A Minnesota State Park Vehicle Permit is required to attend this event.

events.title: Nature Journaling
events.description: Combine creativity and exploration as we take a short stroll through nature. All supplies will be provided for each participant to make their own nature journal, and we will document our observations through guided activities like sound maps and leaf rubbings as we explore the Bear Head Lake trails. This guided activity will start at the Trail Center.
events.address: Bear Head Lake State Park, MN

events.title: Marvelous Mussels- Nature Table
events.description: Wait did that rock just move?! No, it's a mussel! Over 50 species of mussels call Minnesota's waters home, with 40 species found in the St. Croix River. Come explore the diversity of our little-known native mussels and find out their impact on water quality. Drop by the naturalist table on the Riverside Trail past Shelter 1.

events.title: Exploration Station: Pollinator Party
events.description: Drop by the Pollinator Habitat buzzing with excitement. Find Naturalist Mic among the plant beings in the garden area outside the visitor center. Make your own insect inspired by what you find around you. Visit the information table for resources on providing habitat at home or in your community.  If it is raining, stop by the theater inside the visitor center.  Free parking is available in the Wayside Rest lot. This lot is located next to the visitor center.

events.description: Can you tell the difference between an herbivore, omnivore, or carnivore just by looking at their teeth? Would you know which species you are looking at? Stop by the Visitor Center to learn how to tell skulls apart and guess which animals' skulls we have out!

events.title: Discovery Table - The Bear Necessities
events.description: Stop in anytime to learn the bear necessities about how to coexist with bears in the habitat we share with them. We can help protect bears by being careful about how we live in the outdoors!

events.title: Guardians of the Garden
events.description: At the pollinator garden by the Swinging Bridge. Discover how the park's wildflowers rely on bees, butterflies, and other pollinators to thrive. We'll explore the hidden connection between blooms and the creatures that help them grow. Stop in to chat with the naturalist about what's buzzing around our pollinator garden today.

events.description: The St. Louis River flows through Jay Cooke State Park into Lake Superior. Learn all about water, hydroelectricity, and more with Naturalist Dan. Follow the signs across the bridge to his nature program.

events.title: Art in the Park-Fish Prints
events.description: Learn about fish and create a work of art! Gyotaku is the traditional Japanese art of printing fish. Learn about Minnesota fish and then make your own fish prints to take home. This program is for all ages.

events.title: Discovery Table - Plants and Pollinators Palooza
events.description: Buzz over to learn about the adaptations of plants and pollinators that create the beautiful plants we see around the park. Stop in anytime during this ongoing program. The table is set up along the sidewalk to the Swinging Bridge outside the River Inn Visitor Center.

events.title: Mysteries in History: The Picnic Grounds
events.description: Meet at the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds. Have you ever had a picnic in Itasca State Park�s picnic grounds and wondered who had eaten a meal in the same place? What would their view have been? Who would they have seen? What kinds of activities could they have done nearby after lunch? Come along on a hike through this area to visualize and learn more about the buildings both past and present, the previous residents, and how the area came to be the picnic grounds.

events.description: Summer is in full swing! While we shed layers and store our coats, the mammals of Minnesota take a different approach. Stop by The River Inn Visitors Center and explore soft, fuzzy materials with a Park Naturalist and see how many furs you can identify!

events.title: Jr. Naturalist: X Marks the Spot
events.description: Meet the campfire circle outside the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds (In between Lake Itasca and the picnic shelter). Kids, come follow the treasure map and see if X really does mark the spot! Explore different maps and see how they can lead you on your next adventure. Make and take home your very own treasure map and use a map to find hidden treasure.

events.title: The Fern Walk
events.description: Meet at Forest Inn (across from Douglas Lodge). Join the naturalists on a walk in the woods exploring ferns. We are excited to share fern's fascinating double life cycle as well as some ways to identify some of Itasca's common ferns.

events.title: Manoomin: Wild Rice Walk
events.description: Meet at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center. Interested in our Minnesota state grain? Have you ever eaten wild rice and wondered where it came from? Join us as we walk to the Headwaters of the Mississippi River and talk about wild rice, manoomin in Ojibwe. Come see �the good berry� and learn how it is traditionally harvested and processed.

events.title: Wee Wednesdays: Trees
events.description: A kids program! Come listen to Naturalist Dora read a story about the mighty oak tree and stay for a craft! All children must be accompanied by an adult.  Dress for the weather that day. This program will be cancelled in the event of thunderstorms.  While this program is free, there is an entrance fee for the park. A day permit is $7, or an annual permit is $35. They can be purchased online or at the park office.

events.title: Hallaway Hill Hike
events.description: Join Naturalist Dora on a reflective 1.3 mile hike up Hallaway Hill! This will be a relaxed hike stopping occasionally to admire the sights and sounds of the prairie and woodlands as we traverse up the hill.  Maplewood State Park has one track chair that can be checked out for this hike. Please call ahead to the park to reserve it.  The trail is crushed gravel terrain and ADA accessible.  Children must be accompanied by an adult. Comfortable walking shoes, bug spray, sunscreen, and water are all recommended. While this program is free, there is an entrance fee for the park. A day permit is $7,

events.title: Legacy of Lava: Interpretive Walk
events.description: Gooseberry Falls State Park may be known for its beautiful waterfalls, but many less see the ancient lava flow known as the Picnic Flow; a magnificent view that has been 1.1 billion years in the making.  As we walk across bedrock and a grassy lawn to the river, we will travel through time to learn about ancient lava flows and how the landscape has changed since then.  The hike will be ~2/3 of a mile at best.  Expect uneven walking surfaces. It is often very windy next to the lake. Appropriate for all ages.  Meet at Picnic Flow parking lot near the Gitchi-Gami State Bike Trail crossing. This is

events.title: Agate Adventures - Rock Painting
events.description: Paint. Play. Discover. Turn ordinary rocks into extraordinary treasures! Come to the River Inn Visitor Center to learn about the state gemstone and make one to take home! Where to Meet: The River Inn Visitor Center. Who Should Come? Everyone is welcome. This program is for a wide variety of ages.  What to Bring? We will be painting during this program so wear clothes that may become dirty.

events.title: Discovery Table - Take a Look at Bones
events.description: Stop by anytime to hear ongoing mini-talks about some of the animals of the park by looking at their bones. The table is set up near the River Inn Visitor Center.

events.title: Terrific Tree Walk
events.description: From the stately white pine to the lovely smelling balsam fir, there are many incredible trees that make up the boreal forest at Bear Head Lake State Park! Join us for a short talk at the Trail Center to learn about common trees of the park, and practice identifying these trees using tree identification guides.
events.address: Bear Head Lake State Park, MN

events.title: Storytime in Nature- Tree �Bark�
events.description: Meet by the campfire circle outside the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds (in between Lake Itasca and the picnic shelter). Kids, do you like to read stories about nature and the outdoors? Join a naturalist volunteer as we enjoy reading stories outside. After the story, have fun making a craft together that you get to take home. NOTES: Adults must accompany children.

events.title: Kids Explorer Club Nature Hike
events.description: Kids Explorer Club: Nature Hike Adventure Join us for a fun outdoor adventure with the Kids Explorer Club! As we walk along the Pigeon River, we'll use our binoculars and dip nets to explore the wonders of nature. We'll look for birds, insects, wildflowers, and seek out river water creatures along the shoreline. Along the way, we'll practice our observation skills by listening, watching, and discovering the amazing plants and animals that live around us. Bring your walking shoes and a sense of adventure! Runs 2026-08-27 through 2026-08-29.

events.title: Five Facts in Five Minutes: Focus on Field Science
events.description: Near the Mississippi Headwaters (under the porch of the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center if rain). Only have a minute to learn about Itasca State Park? As you visit the Headwaters of the Mississippi River, stop by the nature cart and learn about what takes place at the University of Minnesota's biological field station located in the state park. We will share information about research and education that takes place at this iconic and historic field station.

events.title: Things that go Bump in the Night
events.description: Are you scared of the dark? For many creatures in St Croix State Park, lurking in the dark of night is the key to survival. Come explore the animals who rise when the sun falls and the unique features that allow these critters to thrive in the dark.

events.title: First Timer Fishing
events.description: Learn to fish with Naturalist Dora! Practice casting, learn about lures, hopefully catch a fish, and learn how to release it!  This program is great for all ages. Children must be accompanied by an adult.  Dress for the weather that day. This program will be cancelled in the event of storms or hazardous air quality conditions.  While this program is free, there is an entrance fee for the park. A day permit is $7, or an annual permit is $35. They can be purchased online or at the park office.

events.title: Life on the Edge: Extreme Plants Walk
events.description: Clinging to the park's jaw-dropping cliffs are tenacious and clever plants that have discovered unique ways to survive in habitat where few can. Join the naturalist for a quarter-mile walk past beautiful river scenery and rocky backdrops as we uncover the surprising strategies of these plants, including some that are over a century old. Expect uneven, rocky footing and short sets of stairs. Begin the adventure at the visitor center. Meet outside the park's visitor center. This program takes place entirely outdoors and will be canceled or postponed in the event of lightning or thunder.

events.title: What's in the Water? Macroinvertebrates!
events.description: What's living in Minneopa creek? Learn all about the tiny lives of creatures called macroinvertebrates with the park naturalists. Stop by anytime between 1:00pm-2:00pm to view live tiny critters up close and learn what they can tell us about the health of the creek. Meet the waterfall picnic area.

events.title: Birding for Beginners
events.description: Want to try birding, but don't know where to start? Join the naturalist on the Pondview Trail to learn about some of the birds that call the area home.  For the best experience, binoculars are recommended. Please bring your own binoculars if you have them. We have a limited number of binoculars available for those who do not have their own. Please ask the naturalist to borrow a pair when you arrive for the hike if needed. We will be meeting at the Sibley Interpretive Center and hiking the Pondview Interpretive Trail. It is a 0.7-mile loop with a maximum grade of 7 percent for 190ft.

events.title: Birding for Beginners
events.description: How many times have you seen a bird flying by and wondered what kind of bird it was?  How many species of birds can be seen in Minnesota, or you would like to use a binocular but couldn't figure how to find that hopping bird through it?  It is Spring and many birds are back or passing by.  Come with Fort Snelling State Park's naturalist for a guided bird watching adventure.  Learn the correct techniques of using binoculars and how to adjust binoculars to fit your preference.  We will show you how to identify some of the common bird species from their calls and appearances.  Bird watching is a

events.title: Whose Tracks are these?
events.description: Come explore the exciting world of tracks and other signs animals leave behind. The park is home to a variety of wildlife and many of them have unique feet that help us figure out how they live their lives. We'll make an air-dry clay model of a track to take home. While they dry, we'll explore the unique qualities of the animals in the park by looking at their furs, skulls, and, of course, their feet! We'll be meeting at the Interpretive Classroom located in the downstairs area of the Interpretive Center - Also known as the Trail Center.

events.title: Fish Printing!
events.description: Come join us at the Trail Center to learn about gyotaku, a Japanese art form used to document the fish that were caught. You will get to look at real examples of gyotaku and get to take home your very own fish print! You can stop by anytime from 7-8 p.m. for this activity.
events.address: Bear Head Lake State Park, MN

events.title: Our Great Northern Diver: Tackling Threats to the Common Loon
events.description: Take a dive- deep into the underwater world of the Common Loon. At this exciting sit-down program, you will be dazzled with the skills of loons and how these birds are designed to dive deep and what threats they face in our lakes. Learn how to tackle these threats today!  Located at the outdoor amphitheater by Lady Slipper Lodge. Appropriate for all ages.

There is a small parking lot, but if you're camping, please walk if possible. Seating is available.

Learn to identify common fish species in Minnesota and have the chance to catch some fish. Suitable for ages 6-12.  NOTES: An adult must accompany children. Bring your own fishing pole or use one provided (limited number). Poles are available on first come first serve basis. Bait provided. Non-Minnesota residents will need a fishing license.

events.title: Trees of Itasca, Walk
events.description: Meet at the campfire circle by the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds. Interested in learning about the trees of Itasca? Join the naturalist for a talk and short walk as we discover some of trees and how to identify them.

events.title: Ask a Naturalist - Swinging Bridge Rove
events.description: The naturalist will be roving about the bridge sharing stories and photos about the river and the 100-year-old bridge. Stop in anytime for a short chat. Runs 2026-08-28 through 2026-08-29.

events.title: Discovery Table: Coyotes, American Prairie Wolves
events.description: What's that *yip* chorusing through the night? A uniquely American animal, the coyote is a villainized character in the story of our westward expansion. Are they scoundrels, or the heroes we all need? Stop by the River Inn Visitors Center to learn about this clever creature.

events.title: Nature Walk: Powerful Pollinators
events.description: Discover the beauty and importance of pollinators! Explore blooming wildflowers while observing bees, butterflies, moths, beetles, and other pollinators that help our ecosystems thrive! Learn what we can do to protect them on this half-mile guided walk, suitable for all ages.  Meet at the River Inn Interpretive Center

events.title: Campfire Program - Black Bears of MN
events.description: Although people rarely see them at the park, they are one of the most asked-about animals. Come discover the world of the Minnesota black bear and how to make your outdoor adventures more "bearable." Bench seating. Bring a blanket or camp chair for comfort. Meet at the amphitheater behind the park office.

events.title: St. Croix Sunrise
events.description: Join us to experience the park at daybreak as the sun rises across the St. Croix River and dawn creatures stir. What is it that makes this time of day special?  What changes does the morning bring to the world around us?  Bring a picnic blanket or a camp chair and get ready to explore nature in the wee hours of the day. Flashlight and bug spray recommended. Meet at the St. Croix Lodge.  We will then walk down to the Main Canoe Landing in the campground area.

events.title: New Deal at the Nature Store - CCC Program
events.description: It has been a rough couple years. Many of us have been out of work and in need of aid. Looking for a hand up, not a handout. Come learn about amazing new opportunities to get back to work and make a lasting difference. The passage of the Emergency Conservation Works Act in March of 1933 created thousands of new jobs. After a short presentation the CCC camp superintendent will take prospective enrollees around the grounds to look at examples of the work underway in the park.

events.title: Monarch Butterfly Hike
events.description: Monarchs are beginning to gather for their long flight to Mexico and sometimes flock to the park prairie. Look for some of these amazing pollinators on this guided tour. Meet at the amphitheater. All children must be accompanied by adults.

events.title: Voyageur Canoe Tour: Ducks, Geese & Heritage
events.description: Ride in a 10-person canoe while learning about the history of the area, including ducks and geese that have been hunted in the area for centuries. Participants must be at least 10 years old.  Registration is required and limited to the first 18 people to sign up for each tour. Paddles and life jackets are provided.  To register, email erin.fallon@state.mn.us before 8 a.m. on Saturday, August 29. Include the following info: your name, phone #, time of tour, number of people attending, and children�s ages (if applicable). You will receive a confirmation email to show you successfully registered.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Skin and Bones
events.description: You can learn a lot about an animal from its skeleton and skin. Drop by the naturalist table at the Mount Tom Parking lot to see what you can discover. Activity last about 5 minutes

events.title: Paddle in the Park
events.description: Enjoy the morning on Lake Andrew learning a little bit about the history of the park and the environment around us. This program will be canceled if the windspeed is above 15mph, or if there is thunder or lightening. All participants must be 8 years of age or older and minors must be accompanied by an adult who will be paddling with them. All experience levels are welcome. This program is limited to 6 participants and weather dependent. Please pre-register to reserve your spot by contacting Savannah at savannah.stephenson@state.mn.us Pre-registration ends at 3:00 p.m. on Friday, August 28.  We

events.title: Family Voyageur Canoe Ride
events.description: This ride is for families with smaller children, or for those who just want a short ride in a 10-person canoe.  Participants must weigh at least 40 pounds and sit in their own seat.  Registration is required and limited to the first 18 people to sign up for each tour. Paddles and life jackets are provided.  To register, email erin.fallon@state.mn.us before 8 a.m. on Saturday, August 29. Include the following info: your name, phone #, time of tour, number of people attending, and children�‚’s ages (if applicable). You will receive a confirmation email to show you successfully registered.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Creatures of the Potholes: Investigation Station
events.description: Tons of legs, jet propulsion, or a built-in snorkel!? Drop by to discover the strange adaptations of mysterious creatures that call the park's glacial potholes home. Most participants spend about ten minutes at this ongoing station. Find us outside the park's visitor center.

events.title: Don't Move a Mussel (best for ages 3 to adult)
events.description: The St. Croix River supports an astonishing diversity of native mussels. Hear the story of how some species became endangered. Touch shells of various shapes and discover how they trick fish into raising their babies.  Drop by the Visitor Center anytime during the program. Most people spend about 10 minutes at this station.

events.title: Mini Monsters
events.description: Join our naturalist to learn about the life in the river.  We will use nets and buckets to catch the critters the call the river home. We will see what they can tell us about the water quality of the Whitewater River.
events.address: Whitewater State Park - Visitor Center, MN

events.title: Bats: Echoes in the Night
events.description: Explore the fascinating world of Minnesota's bats! Uncover the secrets of their nocturnal navigation and discover which species call our state home. Join us in unraveling the mysteries of these often-misunderstood mammals! Meet at the amphitheater. This program is free to attend, but a vehicle permit is required for all motor vehicles entering the park. It is $7 for a day or $35 for a 12-month permit. Permits can be purchased online or at the park office.
events.address: Nerstrand Big Woods State Park, MN

events.title: Prairie Palette: A colorful walk through the prairie
events.description: This time of year, the prairie starts to change its colors. Come walk through the prairie in search of a rainbow of colors! Meet at the Sunset Lake Trailhead.  The trail will be a mowed grass trail with relatively even terrain. There are two small hills on the trail that we will be walking up.  Please dress for the weather conditions that day. Feel free to bring binoculars to spot our feathered friends. This program will be cancelled if there are storms or poor air quality conditions.  While this program is free, there is an entrance fee for the park. A day permit is $7, or an annual permit is

events.title: National Toasted Marshmallow Day
events.description: Meet in amphitheater behind park office What happens in the park after the sun goes down? Join us around the campfire for an interactive exploration of the nighttime world. Use your senses to uncover hidden sounds, mysterious scents, fascinating textures, and surprising sights as we discover how both people and wildlife experience the dark. And for our sense of taste, we will be roasting marshmallows!

events.title: Buzzing With Excitement: Guided Wildflower Walk
events.description: Join Park Naturalist Mic on a slow walk around a loop at the Shipwreck Creek Campground, which has been seeded with native flowers found throughout the state of Minnesota. On this hike, less than a mile in length on flat ground, you will gain appreciation for how flowers are perfectly designed to interact with the world around them. Canceled if lightning.   Meet by Shipwreck Creek sanitation building. Mic will be by the picnic bench.
events.address: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park, MN

events.title: Orienteering Scavenger Hunt
events.description: Join us at the Trail Center for an introduction to orienteering, a sport where you use a compass to navigate between two points. We will walk through how to use a compass, and then practice those skills during an animal track scavenger hunt at the beach!
events.address: Bear Head Lake State Park, MN

events.title: Five Facts in Five Minutes: Manoomin (Wild Rice)
events.description: Near the Mississippi Headwaters (at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center if rain.)  Only have a minute to learn about Itasca State Park? Stop at the naturalist station and explore manoomin (wild rice) with Annette Drewes, manoomin (wild rice) researcher as you visit the Headwaters of the Mississippi River.

events.title: Kids' Activity: Fish Printing
events.description: Create beautiful Gyotaku art (fish print) from a soft fish replica!  Look for the Naturalist in the Beach Area, any time within the 2 hours. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.

events.title: Kids' Activity: Fish Printing
events.description: Create beautiful Gyotaku art (fish print) from a soft fish replica! Look for the Naturalist Intern across the parking lot from the Interpretive/Visitor Center any time within the hour. The building is closed due to construction. All programs will take place outdoors. Rain or inclement weather will cancel the program.
events.address: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, MN

events.title: Fungus Among Us (best for ages 8-adult)
events.description: Have you ever walked in the woods a few days after a good rain? Mushrooms are popping up everywhere, but they're only the tip of the iceberg. Join mushroom enthusiasts to discover what's happening below the surface. We'll walk up to a half mile on flat trails (with stops) to find as many fungus species as we can! You'll receive a free mushroom journal to record your findings.   Meet at the Visitor Center at the start time. If you're using a stroller or wheelchair, contact Sean at sean.hoppes@state.mn.us or 651-583-2125 x227 so we can plan an accessible route. Best for ages 8-adult, but all age

You'll receive a free mushroom journal to record your findings.   Meet at the Trail Center at the start time. If you're using a stroller or wheelchair, contact Sean at sean.hoppes@state.mn.us or 651-583-2125 x227 so we can plan an accessible route. Best for ages 8-adult, but all ages welco

events.title: Nocturnal Animals, Campfire
events.description: Meet at the campfire circle by the Lakeside Museum in the picnic grounds. Come learn about some of the nocturnal animals of Itasca State Park! Find out how these animals are adapted to use their senses to be active at night. Remember to bring supplies if you would like to fix some s�mores at our campfire.

events.title: Ask a Naturalist! - Campground Rove
events.description: The naturalist will be roving about the campground answering "What to do?" and "What did I just see?" questions, and handing out fun surprises for the kids. Watch for the naturalist walking the campground loops.

events.title: Fire Shelter Race!
events.description: A fire shelter is the last line of defense a wildland fire fighter has.  People working on prescribed fires carry them too incase of the worst case scenario: getting trapped by a fire.  How fast can you get inside a fire shelter? And how does such thin foil protect people from a fire? Stop by to discover more and even try deploying a shelter yourself. Meet at the St. Croix Lodge.

events.title: Explore Potholes on a Guided Tour
events.description: These potholes aren't what you think! Explore GLACIAL potholes and unique geology on a walk with a park guide. Uncover stories hidden within scenic river views. Discover how massive lava flows, glacial rivers and human interest in the area shaped the impressive landscape. Expect rocky terrain and short stairs on this 1/4-mile walk. This tour is best for ages 6 and up. Meet outside the park's visitor center. This program takes place entirely outdoors and will be canceled or postponed in the event of lightning or thunder.

events.description: These potholes aren't what you think! Explore GLACIAL potholes and unique geology on a walk with a park guide. Uncover stories hidden within scenic river views. Discover how massive lava flows, glacial rivers and human interest in the area shaped the impressive landscape. Expect rocky terrain and short stairs on this 1/4-mile walk.
